newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU too optimistic about Hong Kong handover - MEPs.
newsitem.headline: EU too optimistic about Hong Kong handover - MEPs.

text.p: European Union leaders are far too optimistic about the future of Hong Kong once it reverts to Chinese rule in July, members of the European Parliament said on Wednesday.
"I myself do not share the optimism of the Council or some other commentators," British Conservative Edward Kellet-Bowman told the EU assembly. "We have to be very vigilant."

He was speaking after Dutch European Affairs Minister Michael Patijn told the assembly there was much less concern inside Hong Kong than abroad about the future the Beijing authorities were planning for the territory.
Patijn said he was confident Beijing would allow Hong Kong to retain its current political and economic system after Britain handed the territory back to China.
But British Liberal Graham Watson, who visited Hong Kong last month, insisted there was real fear among Hong Kong's six million citizens about life under Chinese rule.
He pointed out that Beijing had already decided to dissolve Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council.
Instead of putting a rosy gloss on the situation, Watson wanted to see EU states actively contesting the dissolution in the international courts.

The European Parliament is expected to adopt a resolution on Thursday condemning the revocation of the Legislative Council and urging Beijing to respect in every particular the Sino- British Joint Declaration setting out the terms of the handover.
The resolution is also expected to demand free and fair elections in Hong Kong within three months of the return to Chinese sovereignty.

Irish Conservative John Cushnanan said the EU should start preparing trade and other sanctions now, in case China reneged on its commitments to respect Hong Kong's autonomy and freedom of speech, assembly, association and religion.
British Labour Euro-MP Michael Hindley urged EU governments urgently to agree to allow Hong Kong citizens visa-free access to all 15 EU member states.
